data.name: Matithyah
data.gender_notes: Matithyah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Hebrew ‘Mattiyahu’ and the Greek ‘Matthias’. In the Bible, Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as an apostle. The name Matithyah carries the meaning “Friend of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Matithyah usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblematic of faith and devotion to God.
data.etymology: Matithyah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Matithyah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Matithyah is a biblical name with historic roots in Christianity as one of the twelve apostles, alongside Peter, James, and John.
data.spiritual_significance: Matithyah signifies the journey of faith and obedience to God's call, as depicted in the New Testament story of his selection as an apostle.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Matithyah is a Hebrew name derived from the words "Mattithyah," meaning "gift of God," emphasizing the belief in receiving divine guidance and blessings. This name signifies a deep connection to God and trust in His providence.

biblical_reference.note: Matthias was chosen to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles

historical_references.reference: The New Testament of the Bible mentions a disciple named Matthias who was chosen by the apostles to replace Judas Iscariot. This event is detailed in the Acts of the Apostles, chapter 1, verses 12-26.
historical_references.context: After Jesus' death and resurrection, the twelve apostles were tasked with spreading the gospel to the far corners of the earth. When Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus and hanged himself, the apostles needed to choose a new disciple to replace him. They decided to choose by lot, and Matthias was the chosen one.

historical_references.reference: Eusebius of Caesarea, a prominent early Christian historian, writes in his Ecclesiastical History that Matthias was the bishop of Judea. This would have been around the late first or early second century A.D.
historical_references.time_period: Late First Century to Early Second Century A.D.
historical_references.context: Eusebius mentions Matthias as the successor of James, the brother of Jesus, as the bishop of Judea. This suggests that Matthias may have held a position of authority within the early Christian church.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Matithyah' is a modern variation of the biblical name 'Matthew'. It is increasingly seen in New Age spirituality circles and among those who practice Hebraic Christianity and Messianic Judaism. On online forums, YouTube channels, and social media groups, individuals may use the name 'Matithyah' as a way to connect with like-minded individuals, explore spirituality, or deepen their connection to their faith. The use of this name reflects a trend towards a more personal and unique expression of faith, as well as an interest in exploring the Hebrew roots of Christianity.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Matithyah in Jerusalem, Israel credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Matithyah, which means "Friend of God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
